summary: David E. Riggs specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. After completing his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, he taught at UCSB, UIUC, and UH Mānoa, and held research posts at Nichibunken (attested 2006) and Oberlin College (attested 2010).

David Faure is a scholar of Sinology and history. He studied at the University of Hong Kong and earned a PhD from Princeton University. He taught at Indiana University, lectured at St Antony's College (1990), and served as director at CUHK.

David Fiordalis works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Carleton College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Michigan (PhD under Luis O. Gómez). In 2017, he was attested as associate professor and department chair at Linfield University.
David Forbes held academic posts at Brooklyn College as faculty and at the Graduate Center, CUNY, as affiliate faculty, both attested in 2016.
David Friedman was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher. He served as Reader in Indian Philosophy at SOAS (~1950–1965) and as Professor at the University of London (~1950–1970).

David N. Gellner is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. Attested at the University of Oxford in 1988, he is attested in 2026 as Emeritus Professor of Social Anthropology at Oxford and Wolfson College.

David Germano is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992. He joined the University of Virginia, serving as Associate Professor (attested 2000–2008) and faculty member (attested 2026).
David Gonsalez works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He pursued traditional studies under Gen Lobsang Choephel, Lati Rinpoche, Kirti Tsenshab Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

David Gordon White is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at UW-Madison, Paris, Banaras Hindu University, and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1988). He taught at Virginia (1986, 1994–1996) and UCSB from 1996.

David Graeber studied at SUNY Purchase and the University of Chicago (~1984–1996) under Marshall Sahlins. He held academic posts at Yale University (1998–2007), Goldsmiths (2007–2013), and the London School of Economics (~2013–2020).

David Higgins is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held a post at the University of Vienna (attested 2015) and serves as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

David J. Kalupahana was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Ceylon and SOAS/University of London (PhD ~1966). He taught at Ceylon (~1959–1972) and chaired the philosophy department at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa from 1972.

David Jones, a scholar of philosophy and religious studies, earned his PhD at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. Attested in 2007, he was professor of philosophy in the University System of Georgia and director of the Center for the Development of Asian Studies.

David K. Wyatt was a historian who studied at Harvard, Boston University, and Cornell (PhD ~1966). He held posts at SOAS (~1962–1968), Michigan (~1968–1969), and Cornell (1969–2002), where he chaired the history department, later serving as AAS president (1993).
David Kerman Tomlinson specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (attested 2019) under Daniel A. Arnold, and held a post at Smith College.
David Kopf was a scholar of Indology and history. He studied at the University of Chicago (~1958–1964) and spent his academic career at the University of Minnesota (~1967–2003).
David L. Gosling specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall in 1992 and was attested at the University of Cambridge in 2001.

David L. Haberman is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Colorado Boulder. He held posts at the University of Arizona and Indiana University Bloomington (~1993–2021), where he became Professor Emeritus in 2021.

David L. McMahan specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. After teaching at UCSB and the University of Vermont, he served at Franklin & Marshall College as assistant professor (attested 2002) and professor of religious studies (attested 2013).

David Ludden is a historian and Indologist. Educated at Yale and Penn, he held posts at Virginia (1979–1980), Penn (1981–2008), BRAC University (2005), and NYU (starting 2007 as professor of political economy and globalization).
